definition: ICH E9(R1) estimand framework (Step 4, Nov 2019): a treatment effect is defined by five attributes - population, treatment, variable (endpoint), handling of intercurrent events, and population-level summary - specified before any estimator is chosen.
primary_source: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis (2019)
what_it_says_about_this_repo: Prespecification is a solved problem at the level of a guideline. The repository has never applied it: it reports LVEF gains, CRP values and hazard ratios without stating which of them, at what threshold, in whom, is 'the solution'.

definition: T-optimality for model discrimination (Atkinson & Fedorov 1975), and the Bayesian entropy criterion of Box & Hill (1967): choose the design maximising the divergence between rival model predictions, accounting for prediction and observation variance.
what_it_says_about_this_repo: A mature field with tooling (e.g. GPdoemd). The criterion is computable for this model and is applied here.

definition: Structural identifiability analysis: whether parameters are uniquely recoverable from ideal noise-free data, given the model structure and the chosen observables. Established tools include DAISY, SIAN, GenSSI, STRIKE-GOLDD, COMBOS and StructuralIdentifiability.jl.
primary_source: Bellu et al. (2007) DAISY, Comput Methods Programs Biomed
what_it_says_about_this_repo: A mature field. The relevant finding is structural: in a single chain with one observable, the rates are not separately recoverable, and no tool can make them so.

definition: Practical identifiability via profile likelihood (Raue et al. 2009): a parameter can be structurally identifiable yet still practically unidentifiable given the amount and quality of available data. The profile likelihood gives confidence intervals and can be used for experimental planning.
what_it_says_about_this_repo: Solves the practical case and provides the interval. It does not solve the structural case: an infinite confidence interval is the correct answer for a structurally unidentifiable parameter, not a failure of the method.

definition: Sloppy models (Gutenkunst et al. 2007): in essentially every systems-biology model examined, parameter sensitivities span many decades, so behaviour depends on a few stiff combinations. The consequence is a recommendation, not a defect: focus on predictions rather than on parameters.
primary_source: Gutenkunst et al. (2007) PLoS Comput Biol 3:e189
what_it_says_about_this_repo: This is the strongest defence of the repository's position. The literature says parameter non-identifiability is normal and that the response is to validate predictions. The repository has done the first half and none of the second.

definition: TRIPOD+AI (Collins et al. 2024, BMJ 385:e078378) and REMARK (McShane et al. 2005): a prediction model is assessed by discrimination AND calibration on data not used to develop it, reported with confidence intervals. TRIPOD+AI is explicit that internal splits are not external validation.
what_it_says_about_this_repo: The standard exists and is unambiguous. The repository has no held-out dataset, and the guideline explicitly rejects reusing development data as validation.

definition: Surrogate endpoint validation: Prentice's criteria (1989) and the trial-level R2 of Buyse & Molenberghs. In heart failure the evidence is that treatment effects on LVEF explain at most part of the effect on mortality, with an STE of about +6 percentage points and R2 of 0.59.
what_it_says_about_this_repo: The framework is settled and its verdict for this repository is negative: LVEF cannot stand in for mortality, and the effect size sought here is BELOW the surrogate threshold.

definition: Computational reproducibility guidance (e.g. the systems-biology reproducibility survey of Tiwari et al. 2021): 51% of 455 published models reproduced their own published results directly, and 37% could not be rescued even with effort, chiefly through missing parameter values and initial conditions.
primary_source: Tiwari et al. (2021) EMBO Reports, reproducibility in systems biology modelling
what_it_says_about_this_repo: The measured baseline is that roughly half of published models do not reproduce. This repository reproduces its own legacy script to three decimals and types every constant - so it is ahead of the baseline, but it has never reproduced an independently published result.
